name: Jaipur–Kishangarh Expressway

tollInfo.note: This road is tolled. Indian toll rates are revised every year on 1 April, so check the current notification before you travel.

history: The Jaipur–Kishangarh stretch of the Delhi–Ahmedabad highway was one of the first six-lane tolled roads built in Rajasthan under a private concession, opening in 2005. It runs across flat, dry country from Jaipur towards Ajmer, and it set the pattern for the six-laning of the rest of NH 48.
facts: One of the earliest six-lane tolled highway sections in Rajasthan.
Part of NH 48, the Delhi–Jaipur–Ahmedabad–Mumbai route and one of India's busiest freight corridors.
Kishangarh, at its western end, is the centre of India's marble trade.
It carries most road traffic between Jaipur and Ajmer, including pilgrims to the Ajmer Sharif dargah and Pushkar.
significance: This is a link in the road chain between Delhi and Mumbai, and the main route from Jaipur towards Ajmer, Pushkar and Udaipur. Marble lorries from Kishangarh and freight from Gujarat run on it day and night.
